newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies expected lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open 0.100 to 0.200 cent a lb lower while pork bellies were called 0.100 to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Weakness in cash hogs and further declines in pork cutout values will likely weigh on hog futures at the start. However, futures could easily rally as packer demand is expected to strengthen for hogs late this week to meet needs for planned large Saturday kills, analysts said.
Cash pork prices are expected to be underpinned by late September and into October by National Pork Month retail pork featuring which will provide support, they said.

Pork belly futures were expected to show carryover weakness after prices fell late Tuesday. The relatively brisk slaughter pace so far this week and weak tone to cash bellies will likely weigh on the market as will a weak technical picture, they said.
USDA estimated week-to-date hog slaughter through Tuesday at 714,000 head. The figure was not comparable with last week because of the Labor Day holiday but was above the year-ago figure of 706,000.
Although the CME out-of-town report was considered mildly constructive to futures, the weak trend to cash bellies will likely outweigh effects of the report, they said.
CME reported the weekly out-of-town net movement at out 1.684 million lbs compared with pre-report estimates of out 0.5 million to 0.75 million lbs.
